_readme: Behavioral golden set (design §10.2) — this file encodes the WHOLE POINT of hierarchical search: asymmetric net width. Run via scripts/run_golden_queries.py against a dev DB after backfill. Fields: query; expect_includes / expect_excludes = canonical titles asserted against the response's RelatedTitles + Resolved block; expect_resolves_to = asserted against Resolved.CanonicalTitle; expect_same_results_as = assert full result-set equality with that query; expect_seniority = asserted against the applied facet. TODO(you): grow this to ~30 cases as the taxonomy fills in — every bug you fix by hand should land here as a case first.

_note: WIDE net: the generic family query pulls in every specialization
NARROW net — the heart of the feature: generic 'software engineer' postings have specs={} which does NOT contain {backend}, so they are EXCLUDED. No symmetric-similarity system can pass this case.
equivalence: identical plan → assert full result-set equality, not just overlap
typo tolerance via fuzzy match on title_map keys (§9.1 step 2) — must clear fuzzyAcceptFloor
seniority is a FACET, not title identity: same plan as 'backend engineer' plus the seniority filter
MLE is its own family (§5.2 policy) — a 'software engineer' search means generalist SWE, not MLE
